notes.text: Bake the chips on two sheet pans, and warm the beans in the large pot.

move.title: Three parts, one finish
move.body: Ful medames is fava beans warmed and mashed with cumin, lemon, and olive oil, eaten across Egypt for breakfast. It comes with baked pita chips and a cucumber and tomato salad. The skill is timing: the slowest part starts first, so all three are ready together.

why.title: Slowest first
why.body: The oven takes 10 minutes to heat and the chips 10 more to bake. The salad takes about 10 minutes to cut, and the beans 5 minutes to warm. So the oven goes on first, the salad gets cut while it heats, and the beans warm while the chips bake.

why.title: Measure before the heat
why.body: Once the beans are warm, there's no time to look for the cumin. Measure everything into small bowls before the stove goes on.

why.title: Warm, not boiled
why.body: The beans are already cooked. Medium-low heat warms them through without sticking or spattering.

why.title: Mash some, not all
why.body: Mashing about half the beans with a fork makes them creamy, and the whole ones keep some bite.

why.title: Dress the salad last
why.body: Salt pulls water out of cucumber and tomato. Dressed just before serving, the salad stays crisp.

wrong.sign: The chips are pale and soft
wrong.fix: Bake them 2 or 3 minutes more. They crisp more as they cool.

wrong.sign: The beans are sticking to the pan
wrong.fix: Turn the heat down and stir in 2 tablespoons of water.

wrong.sign: The beans were ready long before the chips
wrong.fix: Next time, start the beans when the chips go in, not before.
Pour off the liquid. Next time, add the salt and lemon just before serving.

choices: The slowest one, the oven and chips

quiz.q: Why measure the spices before the stove goes on?
choices: There's no time once the beans are warm
quiz.explain: Everything in its place, like week 3.

quiz.q: Why warm the beans on medium-low?
choices: They're already cooked and only need warming
quiz.explain: Higher heat makes them stick and spatter.

quiz.q: When does the salad get its salt and lemon?

ingredients.prep: half for the salad, half for the beans

substitutions.note: Corn tortilla chips bake the same way. Check them at 7 minutes.

steps.text: Read the recipe. Notice the order: oven first, then the salad, then the beans while the chips bake.
steps.tip: Halving or doubling? Write down the new amounts now.

steps.text: Move a rack to the middle while the oven is cold. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Measure the beans' olive oil, garlic, cumin, and salt into a small bowl. Set it by the stove.
steps.look: Everything for the beans in one bowl, ready.

steps.text: Cut each pita into 8 wedges with the paring knife, like a pizza. Spread them on the sheet pan.
Brush the wedges with the chips' olive oil and sprinkle with the chips' salt.
steps.tip: Both sides crisp better, but one side is fine.

steps.text: Halve the cucumber the long way with the bridge grip. Slice it into half-moons with the claw grip.
Halve each tomato with the bridge grip, then cut each half into 4 wedges. Add them to the medium bowl with the cucumber.
steps.tip: Saw gently so the tomato doesn't squash.

steps.text: Cut the lemon in half. Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade away from you.
When the oven is hot, put on mitts and slide in the chips.
steps.look: Golden at the edges and crisp.

steps.text: Open the beans and pour them, liquid and all, into the saucepan. Set it on a back burner, handle in.
Warm the beans over medium-low heat, stirring now and then.
steps.look: Steaming, with small bubbles at the edges.

steps.text: Turn off the burner. Stir in the measured bowl, squeeze in half the lemon, and mash about half the beans with the fork.
Mitts on. Pull the rack out, lift out the pan, and set it on the stovetop. Turn off the oven.
steps.tip: The chips crisp more as they cool.

steps.text: Squeeze the other lemon half over the salad, add the salad's salt, and toss with the spoon.
Spoon the beans into bowls. Serve with the pita chips for scooping and the salad on the side.
steps.tip: A spoonful of olive oil on top of the beans is traditional.
